- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.18) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; apply downward correction of 1–3% to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment is rising (≥0.36) and model is flat or slightly rising, model underestimates; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% to align with sentiment momentum.
- Model frequently overpredicts in early horizon (1–3 days) when sentiment is neutral or slightly negative; apply 0.5–1.5% downward bias for first 3 days.
- Mean reversion bias: if model forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence; if below, increase by 0.5–1% per day.
- Sentiment + price divergence: if sentiment is positive but price is flat or falling, model tends to overcorrect; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% to avoid “sentiment-driven overbought” trap.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts often overestimate by 1–3% in early 10–15 days; apply 0.5–1% downward adjustment for first 10 days of forecast.
